sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Socio-Economic Impact of British Rule** in India covering land revenue systems, deindustrialization, drain of wealth, and social reforms.
Spanning from the **Battle of Plassey (1757)** to **Indian Independence (1947)**, with core economic exploitation peaking in the **19th and 20th centuries**.
Entire **British India** including Bengal, Madras, Bombay presidencies, United Provinces (UP), and princely states through indirect control.
British East India Company (EIC) initially, followed by the **British Crown** post-1858, alongside Indian reformers and nationalist leaders.
Crucial core syllabus topic for **UPSSSC PET**; questions regularly appear on land systems, Drain Theory, and social acts.
**Permanent Settlement (1793)**, **Ryotwari System (1820)**, **Mahalwari System (1822)**, **Dadabhai Naoroji's Drain Theory**, and **Western Education Policies**.
Direct factual questions on governors-general, years of land settlements, authors of books, and social reform years.
Introduction of railways (**1853**), telegraph, commercialization of agriculture, and destruction of traditional handicraft industries.

items.title: 1. Land Revenue Systems: Permanent, Ryotwari, Mahalwari
items.content:
• **Permanent Settlement (Zamindari):** Introduced by **Lord Cornwallis** in **1793** in **Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa** (covered 19% of British India).
• **Ryotwari System:** Introduced by **Thomas Munro** and **Captain Read** in **1820** in **Madras, Bombay, and Assam** (covered 51% of British India); direct settlement with cultivators (Ryots).
• **Mahalwari System:** Introduced by **Holt Mackenzie** in **1822** and modified by **Lord William Bentinck** in **1833** in **North-West Provinces (UP), Punjab, and Central India** (covered 30% of British India).
• **Mnemonic for Land Revenue Founders:** **C-M-H** -> **C**ornwallis (Permanent), **M**unro (Ryotwari), **H**olt Mackenzie (Mahalwari).

items.title: 2. Drain of Wealth and Economic Exploitation
items.content:
• **Dadabhai Naoroji:** Known as the **Grand Old Man of India**, propounded the **Drain Theory** in his book **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'** (**1901**).
• **Paper Presented:** First propounded in a paper titled **'England's Debt to India'** in **1867** at the East India Association.
• **Components of Drain:** Home charges, civil and military administrative expenses, interest on public debt, and profits of foreign capitalists.
• **Economic Impact:** Forced transformation of India into a supplier of raw materials and consumer of British manufactured goods.

items.title: 3. Deindustrialization and Commercialization of Agriculture
items.content:
• **Deindustrialization:** Systematic destruction of traditional Indian handicrafts and cottage industries due to **one-way free trade policy** favoring British machine-made goods.
• **Commercialization of Agriculture:** Shift from food crops to cash crops (**indigo, cotton, jute, opium, sugarcane**) driven by British industrial needs and heavy cash revenue demands.
• **Impact of Commercialization:** Made peasants vulnerable to global price fluctuations, market intermediaries, and severe famines (**Great Famine of 1876-78**, **Bengal Famine of 1943**).

items.title: 4. Growth of Modern Education and Press
items.content:
• **Charter Act of 1813:** Allocated **1 Lakh rupees** annually for the revival of literature and promotion of science in India.
• **Macaulay's Minute (1835):** Championed **English Education Act 1835**, promoting Western education through English to create a class of clerks.
• **Wood's Despatch (1854):** Known as the **Magna Carta of English Education in India**; recommended universities in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras (**1857**).
• **Vernacular Press Act (1878):** Enacted by **Lord Lytton** to gag the native press; repealed by **Lord Ripon** in **1882**.

items.title: 5. Social and Religious Reform Movements
items.content:
• **Brahmo Samaj:** Founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in **1828**; campaigned against **Sati** (abolished in **1829** by Lord William Bentinck) and idolatry.
• **Arya Samaj:** Founded by **Swami Dayananda Saraswati** in **1875** with the slogan **'Back to the Vedas'**.
• **Abolition Acts:** **Female Infanticide Acts (1795, 1804)**, **Sati Regulation XVII (1829)**, **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (1856)** passed due to efforts of **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**, and **Age of Consent Act (1891)**.
• **Mnemonic for Social Reform Acts:** **S-W-R** -> **S**ati (**1829**), **W**idow Remarriage (**1856**), **R**eligious Disabilities Act (**1850**).

items.term: Trick 2: Dadabhai Naoroji's Drain Theory Book
items.definition: Book name is **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'** (**1901**). Mnemonic: **P**oor **U**ncle **D**adabhai wrote about **Drain**.
Sati (**1829**) -> Female Infanticide Banned (**1870 Act**) -> Widow Remarriage (**1856**) -> Age of Consent (**1891**). Mnemonic: **S**ati's **W**edding **A**ge (**1829, 1856, 1891**).
Charter Act (**1813**) -> Macaulay Minute (**1835**) -> Wood's Despatch (**1854**) -> Hunter Commission (**1882**). Mnemonic: **C-M-W-H** (**C**at **M**akes **W**ool **H**at).

items.term: Trick 5: Viceroy Lytton vs Ripon Press Policies
items.definition: **L**ytton **L**ocked the Press (**Vernacular Press Act 1878**); **R**ipon **R**eleased the Press (**Repealed 1882**). Match **L** with **L**ock and **R** with **R**elease.
Brahmo = **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** (Brahma is supreme Roy), Arya = **Dayananda** (Dayananda chanted Arya slogans), Satyashodhak = **Phule** (Phule/Flowers for truth). Use keyword association.
Students often confuse Permanent Settlement with Ryotwari. Permanent Settlement was mainly in **Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa**, NOT Madras or Bombay.
Students sometimes attribute Drain Theory to R.C. Dutt or M.G. Ranade. While they contributed, **Dadabhai Naoroji** is the primary propounder and author of 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
Do not confuse **1829** (Regulation XVII abolishing Sati) with **1828** (Year Brahmo Samaj was founded).
Mahalwari system was implemented in **North-West Provinces (UP), Punjab, and Central India**, NOT in Bengal where Zamindari prevailed.
Wood's Despatch was issued in **1854**, whereas universities established under its recommendation came up in **1857** (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras).
The Vernacular Press Act was passed by **Lord Lytton in 1878**, but it was repealed by **Lord Ripon in 1882**, NOT Lord Lytton.
British rule transformed India's self-sufficient village economy into a colonial agrarian appendage of British industrial capitalism.
Introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal; created a new class of landlords (**Zamindars**) who extracted maximum rent from peasants.
Introduced by Thomas Munro in Madras and Bombay; established direct revenue settlement with cultivators (**Ryots**).
Introduced in North-West Provinces and Punjab; revenue assessment was done collectively for the village (**Mahal**).
One-way free trade policy and influx of cheap British machine-made goods ruined Indian handloom weavers and artisans.
Forced shift toward cash crops like **indigo, cotton, and opium** linked Indian agriculture to global market crashes and frequent famines.
Propounded by **Dadabhai Naoroji**; exposed how uncompensated wealth was siphoned off from India to Britain.
Introduction of **Railways (1853)**, telegraph, and postal systems primarily served British military and commercial interests.
Charter Act (**1813**) and Macaulay's Minute (**1835**) promoted English education to supply literate clerks for colonial administration.
Abolition of Sati (**1829**), Widow Remarriage Act (**1856**), and banning of female infanticide reformed traditional social evils.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact years of land revenue systems (1793, 1820, 1822) and the Governors-General associated with them.
Questions often mix up who introduced the Ryotwari system. Remember Thomas Munro and Captain Read in Madras, NOT Lord Cornwallis.
Make a quick summary table of Social Reformers, their organizations, and founding years as UPSSSC regularly asks matching questions.
Do not confuse Dadabhai Naoroji's Drain Theory book name with R.C. Dutt's 'Economic History of India'.

keyTakeaways: Permanent Settlement covered 19%, Ryotwari 51%, and Mahalwari 30% of British India.
Dadabhai Naoroji propounded the Drain Theory in his 1901 book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
Lord William Bentinck abolished Sati in 1829 with the help of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
Wood's Despatch of 1854 is known as the Magna Carta of English Education in India.
Commercialization of agriculture led to extreme vulnerability of Indian peasants during global famines.
Lord Ripon repealed the infamous Vernacular Press Act in 1882 and introduced Local Self-Government.
